narrative:
The model estimates you have a 41% chance of leaving your job, which is high enough that the company has decided to deny your promotion. This prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your profile.

Your relatively short overall work experience of just 1-5 years was the strongest factor pulling the prediction toward leaving. Among employees the model expected to stay, only about half had similarly limited experience, while many had 6-10 years or more. This limited tenure signals higher turnover risk to the system.

The fact that you have not received other job offers while at the company was the second most important influence, and it actually pushed the prediction slightly toward staying. Most employees the model sees as likely to remain also report no external opportunities, so this is a stabilizing element in your case.

However, your third major factor worked against you: finding it difficult to get involved in decision-making and having your opinions heard at work. This pushed the prediction noticeably toward leaving. Only 10% of employees predicted to stay described their involvement as difficult, compared to the majority who find it at least medium.

Taken together, your limited experience and low sense of voice at work outweighed the positive stabilizing effect of having no other offers. The organization should consider giving you clearer opportunities to contribute ideas and more structured ways to build experience quickly. You may want to discuss concrete steps for greater involvement in projects that matter to you.
